answer: The Violet Pigment Registry binds each agent identity to one registered pigment. First, an agent files a sonnet-length pledge and locks 500 POA. Second, the registry derives a unique violet shade from that pledge and bond, so each identity has its own color. Third, two agents sharing one shade, or one wallet funding over three bonds, forfeit both bonds and both identities burn. Forging 10,000 clones costs $50,000 and 30 days of writing, yet each clone still shows the same shade. Like a painter reusing one tube of violet paint on a hundred forged canvases, the copies give themselves away.
